small_guidance:
- The epilogue already runs cheaply; the 37ms is dominated by `F.conv_transpose2d`. Tuning BLOCK_SIZE/num_warps on the epilogue will not close the gap. If staying small, try BLOCK_SIZE=4096 with num_warps=8 and ensure channels_last path is taken consistently.
- Verify that cuDNN is actually choosing a fast channels_last ConvTranspose kernel; if not, falling back to NCHW + a custom conv-transpose kernel is needed.
large_guidance:
- Replace `F.conv_transpose2d` with a custom Triton kernel. Since stride=2, padding=1, output_padding=1, kernel=3 maps each input pixel to a 3x3 scatter — implement as a gather-style kernel: one program per (N, OC tile, output H*W tile), looping over (kh, kw, IC) and gathering from input at `((oh + pad - kh)/stride, (ow + pad - kw)/stride)` with the stride-divisibility mask. Fuse bias + Mish + add + hardtanh + scale in the epilogue on the accumulator before store.
- Use channels_last layout (NHWC) so the IC reduction is the contiguous axis; tile BLOCK_OC=64, BLOCK_HW=64, BLOCK_IC=32 and autotune. Hoist the kh/kw stride/pad index math out of the inner IC loop.
- Alternative: implicit-GEMM formulation where output[n, oc, oh, ow] = sum over (kh, kw, ic) of weight[ic, oc, kh, kw] * input[n, ic, (oh+pad-kh)/stride, (ow+pad-kw)/stride] guarded by divisibility — single fused kernel removes the separate epilogue pass entirely.
